brief: Siegel reads the softer September jobs report as constructive beneath the headline: payroll growth missed and prior months were revised down, but participation rose, the workweek held, manufacturing added 70,000 to 75,000 jobs since January, and U6 fell even as the unemployment rate ticked up. That ambiguity, plus soft wage pressure and stabilizing oil near $90 to $100 WTI, gives the Fed room to pause in October, with a more aggressive move possible in December if inflation forces it. The bigger equity risk is real rates: the 30-year TIPS yield near 3.4% against a roughly 20x market, a 5% earnings yield, leaves only a 1.6-point equity risk premium. Yet the S&P 500 and Nasdaq sit near highs, because earnings optimism, especially continuing AI capital spending with no slowdown, is outweighing that headwind. Higher real rates hit value harder than high-margin tech and growth firms, reversing the earlier value broadening, and Siegel expects tech and growth leadership to persist while real rates stay elevated. With the Fed able to pause, oil stable and spending strong, he stays constructive on equities despite the real-yield headwind.
